findings.description: No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so objects in the reports bucket (including the uploaded vendor roster) are stored without an enforced bucket-default SSE-KMS policy.

findings.issue_category: no public access block or ACL
findings.description: This bucket sets neither an explicit private ACL nor an aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block, so there is no guardrail preventing public object ACLs or a public bucket policy from exposing archived report data.
No logging block is configured, so access to the archived reports and the vendor roster object is not recorded, hampering detection and forensics of unauthorised access.
Versioning is not enabled and force_destroy = true, so objects can be overwritten or destroyed with the bucket without recovery, removing tamper-evidence for stored data.
The ledger export bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration, so sensitive financial export data is stored without enforced default encryption at rest.
The bucket relies solely on a private ACL; without aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block there is no guardrail against a subsequent public bucket policy or object ACL exposing ledger data.
No logging block is configured, so reads and writes of financial export data leave no access audit trail.
The model artifacts bucket enables versioning and logging but defines no default server-side encryption, so artifacts are stored unencrypted by default.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block guards this bucket against public ACLs or bucket policies being applied to model artifacts.
Operational runbooks, which commonly contain internal infrastructure detail and occasionally secrets, are stored in a bucket with no default server-side encryption configured.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is associated with the runbooks bucket, so public ACLs or policies are not blocked at the bucket level.
No logging block is defined, so access to internal operational documentation is not recorded for audit or incident response.

The central log destination bucket uses the log-delivery-write ACL but has no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block, leaving no guardrail against collected access logs being made publicly readable by a later ACL or policy change.
force_destroy = true with no object lock or MFA delete means the authoritative access-log store can be deleted wholesale, defeating the non-repudiation and forensic value of the audit trail.

A vendor roster spreadsheet is uploaded with no kms_key_id or server_side_encryption argument into a bucket that also has no default encryption, so potentially sensitive third-party data is stored in cleartext.

The object is sourced from resources/vendor-roster.xlsx inside the Terraform repository, meaning potentially sensitive vendor data is stored in version control alongside the infrastructure code and distributed to everyone with repo access.
